nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite sets carrying σ-algebras in which singletons are measurable, and let $p$ be a joint probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$. The information gain of $p$ is zero if and only if $p$, as a measure, equals the product of its marginal law on $\alpha$ and its marginal law on $\beta$; that is, exactly when the attribute (first coordinate) and the label (second coordinate) are independent.
nodes.title: Zero information gain means independence

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a joint probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$ with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ finite, and let $p_X$ and $p_Y$ be its marginal laws on $\alpha$ and on $\beta$. Writing $H$ for Shannon entropy in bits, the information gain of $p$ equals $H(p_X) + H(p_Y) - H(p)$.
nodes.title: Information gain in terms of entropies

nodes.summary: For every joint probability law $p$ on $\alpha \times \beta$ with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ finite, the information gain of $p$ is at least $0$.
nodes.title: No split has negative information gain

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a joint probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$ with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ finite, the law of an attribute $X$ (first coordinate) and a label $Y$ (second coordinate). The information gain of splitting on $X$ for predicting $Y$ is the real number $H(Y) - H(Y \mid X)$, where $H(Y)$ is the Shannon entropy in bits of the marginal law of $Y$ and $H(Y \mid X)$ is the conditional entropy in bits of $Y$ given…
nodes.title: Information gain of a split

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite sets carrying σ-algebras in which singletons are measurable, and let $p$ be a joint probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$. The information gain of $p$, regarded as an element of $[0, \infty]$, equals the mutual information in bits of $p$ viewed as a probability measure on $\alpha \times \beta$.
nodes.title: Information gain is mutual information

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
